The Better Auth team took over Auth.js in September 2025, and the project is now in maintenance mode for existing users.

- **The handover:** Better Auth announced on September 22, 2025 that it would maintain and oversee Auth.js ([6-1]). Auth.js was previously called NextAuth.js ([6-1]).
- **Existing users:** Better Auth said current users can keep using Auth.js, and it will keep shipping security patches and urgent fixes ([6-13]). Another summary calls the project "security-patch mode" ([3-12]).
- **New projects:** Better Auth recommends that new projects start with Better Auth instead, except where Auth.js offers a feature Better Auth lacks, such as stateless sessions without a database ([6-14]).
- **v5 status:** next-auth v5 has never reached a stable release. It sits at 5.0.0-beta.32, and the npm latest tag is still v4 ([5-7], [5-8]).
- **Recent security work:** In July 2026, Better Auth's maintainers closed four advisories across @auth/core, next-auth v4 and next-auth v5, and listed the patched versions ([7-3], [7-4]).
- **Ownership:** One source says Vercel acquired Better Auth in July 2026, so both projects now share an owner ([5-6]). Another gives a July 7, 2026 date for that deal ([9-8]). I found only these two sources for it, so treat the date as unconfirmed.

Links: [{"title":"better-auth vs NextAuth vs Clerk — Authentication Comparison 2026","url":"https://supastarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-nextauth-vs-clerk"},{"title":"Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth: Which Authentication for Next.js SaaS in 2026","url":"https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk"},{"title":"better auth vs clerk vs nextauth vs auth js 2026 best authentication for next js","url":"https://ldap.kayako.com/better-auth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-auth-js-2026-best-authentication-for-next-js.html"},{"title":"better auth vs clerk vs nextauth vs auth js best authentication for next 2026","url":"https://ldap.kayako.com/better-auth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-auth-js-best-authentication-for-next-2026.html"},{"title":"Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth (2026)","url":"https://www.turbostarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-supabase-auth"},{"title":"# Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth: Which Authentication for Next.js SaaS in 2026","url":"https://makerkit.dev/blog/md/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk"},{"title":"best auth library nextjs 2026","url":"https://blog.logrocket.com/best-auth-library-nextjs-2026/"},{"title":"better auth vs clerk vs nextauth vs auth js best authentication for next js apps in 2025","url":"https://ldap.kayako.com/better-auth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-auth-js-best-authentication-for-next-js-apps-in-2025.html"},{"title":"ultimate next js auth comparison 2025 betterauth vs clerk vs nextauth vs auth js","url":"https://ldap.kayako.com/ultimate-next-js-auth-comparison-2025-betterauth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-auth-js.html"}]

Most 2026 sources recommend Better Auth for new Next.js projects, with Supabase Auth as the alternative if you already use Supabase. Clerk and Auth.js are framed as narrower choices. These are mostly vendor-adjacent blog posts, so treat the rankings as opinion.

- **Better Auth:** Reviewers call it a TypeScript-native library that stores users in your own Postgres and has strong multi-tenancy support. One review says it has the most complete feature set, including 2FA, passkeys, RBAC, and impersonation. The tradeoff is that you own security updates. Better Auth shipped v1 in early 2025.
- **Auth.js (NextAuth v5):** It is the most established option, but one reviewer argues it is a legacy library most teams keep only because they already use it. It lacks built-in 2FA, passkeys, and RBAC. Auth.js v5 hit stable in late 2024 as a near-complete rewrite. One source says it is now under Better Auth Inc., which I could not confirm elsewhere.
- **Clerk:** It is a hosted service with pre-built UI. Its cost is the main criticism. One review says it gets expensive past 50,000 MAU and locks your user data in a US database. Another lists pricing as Hobby free, then Pro at $25/mo plus $0.02/MRU over 50k.
- **Supabase Auth:** Recommended if you are already on Supabase, since Row Level Security can do half your authorization work for you.

A security point applies to all options: CVE-2025-29927, disclosed in March 2025, showed that middleware-only session protection in Next.js is bypassable by spoofing a header. Check sessions in your server code, not only in middleware.

Some search results were low-quality SEO pages with no substantive content, so I ignored them. A search for the Auth.js-to-Better-Auth relationship from an official source would confirm that claim.

title: proxy.js
description: API reference for the proxy.js file.
related:
  title: Learn more about Proxy
  links:
    - app/api-reference/functions/next-request
    - app/api-reference/functions/next-response
---

> **Note**: The `middleware` file convention is deprecated and has been renamed to `proxy`. See [Migration to Proxy](#migration-to-proxy) for more details.

The `proxy.js|ts` file is used to write [Proxy](/docs/app/getting-started/proxy) and run code on the server before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly.

Proxy executes before routes are rendered. It's particularly useful for implementing custom server-side logic like authentication, logging, or handling redirects.

> **Good to know**:
>
> Proxy is meant to be invoked separately of your render code and in optimized cases deployed to your CDN for fast redirect/rewrite handling, you should not attempt relying on shared modules or globals.
>
> To pass information from Proxy to your application, use [headers](#setting-headers), [cookies](#using-cookies), [rewrites](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#rewrite), [redirects](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#redirect), or the URL.

Create a `proxy.ts` (or `.js`) file in the project root, or inside `src` if applicable, so that it is located at the same level as `pages` or `app`.

If you’ve customized [`pageExtensions`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/pageExtensions), for example to `.page.ts` or `.page.js`, name your file `proxy.page.ts` or `proxy.page.js` accordingly.

```tsx filename="proxy.ts" switcher
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'

// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```

```js filename="proxy.js" switcher
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'

// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
export function proxy(request) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```

## Exports

### Proxy function

The file must export a single function, either as a default export or named `proxy`. Note that multiple proxy from the same file are not supported.

content.text:
I added email and password sign up and sign in, plus Google sign-in, using Better Auth. `/dashboard` now redirects to `/sign-in` unless you're signed in.

I tested it against a local dev server: lint and build pass, and so do the flows below.
- **Protected dashboard:** an unauthenticated request to `/dashboard` redirects (307) to `/sign-in`.
- **Sign up:** signing up creates a session and the dashboard shows the new user.
- **Wrong password:** it returns a clean error.
- **Sign out:** after signing out, `/dashboard` redirects again.
- **Google:** the sign-in endpoint returns a Google OAuth URL, but I couldn't try the actual Google login without real credentials.

## Why Better Auth
- **Auth.js:** it was taken over by the Better Auth team in September 2025 and is now in maintenance mode, with next-auth v5 still in beta. [Better Auth](https://www.better-auth.com/blog/authjs-joins-better-auth) recommends Better Auth for new projects.
- **Clerk:** it's a hosted service that gets expensive at scale, and your user data sits with them.
- **Better Auth:** it's TypeScript-native, keeps users in your own database, and has first-class Next.js support. Most 2026 comparisons I found recommend it for new Next.js projects. Those comparisons are mostly vendor-adjacent blogs, so treat the rankings as opinion.

Sources: [Better Auth vs NextAuth vs Clerk](https://supastarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-nextauth-vs-clerk), [Makerkit comparison](https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk), [Auth.js joins Better Auth](https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/discussions/13252).

## What changed
- **`src/lib/auth.ts`:** the Better Auth config, with email and password enabled (8-character minimum) and Google, stored in SQLite via `src/lib/db.ts`.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`:** `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real session, replacing the "first user" TODO. `listUsers()` and `getUser()` now read Better Auth's `user` table instead of the hardcoded list, so the two seed users, Ada and Grace, are gone.
- **`src/proxy.ts`:** this is the Next 16 name for middleware. It redirects unauthenticated requests to `/dashboard` to `/sign-in`.
- **Dashboard:** it re-checks the session itself and redirects if there isn't one, because proxy-only protection has been bypassed before (CVE-2025-29927). I also added a sign-out button.
- **UI:** new `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` pages and the auth API route.
- **`.env.example`:** placeholders for the auth secret, base URL, Google client ID and secret, and database path. I added `!.env.example` to `.gitignore`, because `.env*` was ignoring it.

## To run it
1. `cp .env.example .env.local`, generate a secret with `openssl rand -base64 32`, and add real Google credentials. Set the redirect URI to `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google`.
2. `npm run auth:migrate` creates the tables.
3. `npm run dev`.

## Things to know
- **Database:** the SQLite file lives on local disk, so it won't work on serverless hosts like Vercel. Swap `src/lib/db.ts` for Postgres there.
- **Team list:** the dashboard's "Team" list shows every registered user to any signed-in user. That matches the old behavior, but it's worth revisiting for a public app.
- **Email verification:** it isn't required, so people can sign up with any email address.
- **Generated files:** Next generated `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` in the project root. I left them untracked.
- **Commit:** nothing is committed yet.
